CC 7. Endorse the accuracy of information presented in Lancaster Choice Energyâ€™s (LCE) 2016 Power Content Label based on staffâ€™s review and independent auditor report.
California Public Utilities Code requires all retail sellers of electric energy, including Lancaster Choice Energy (LCE), to disclose â€œaccurate, reliable, and simple-to-understand information on the sources of energyâ€ that are delivered to their respective customers. Applicable regulations direct retail sellers to provide such communications no later than October 1st of each year. The format for requisite communications is highly prescriptive, offering little flexibility to retail sellers when presenting such information to customers. This format has been termed the â€œPower Content Labelâ€ by the California Energy Commission (CEC). To fulfill its Power Content Label reporting obligation, LCE must also provide the CEC with Councilâ€™s attestation regarding the accuracy of information included in the Power Content Label. While developing LCEâ€™s 2016 Power Content Label, staff along with technical consultants performed a detailed review of all power purchases completed for the 2016 calendar year. Subsequent to this review, a third party auditor verified that the content contained within the report to the CEC was accurate.

CC 8. Approve an increase in the purchase amount of Bid No. 642-16, Emulsified Asphalt Materials, to VSS Emultech in support of the Cityâ€™s Revive 25 Pavement Management Program.
Over the next ten months, the City anticipates it will treat 175 lane miles of roads utilizing a variety of pavement preservation treatments. This is a significant increase from the number of roads that staff originally planned on treating during that timeframe. The City decided it would be in its best interest to accelerate several internal road projects due to the anticipated price increase in raw materials and road construction costs that will begin next year. The escalation can be attributed to the increase of transportation funding that cities will begin to receive from the passage of SB 1 legislation and Measure R tax increase.

CC 9. Approve an increase in the purchase amount of Bid No. 661-17, Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement Screening Materials, to Reclaimed Aggregates Inc., for the Revive 25 Pavement Management Program.
By increasing the purchase amount of reclaimed asphalt now, it will allow the City to lock in competitive bid pricing before material prices increase next year. It will also allow the City to maximize the number of roads being treated over the next year, utilizing its current pavement management budget.

Approve Multi-Year Professional Service Agreements with each of the pre-qualified consulting firms for labor compliance services for public works projects, and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents and execute all task orders within existing signature authority limits.
In July 2017, the City advertised Request for Qualifications (RFQ 667-17) for Labor Compliance Services to support the Capital Improvement Program on all public works projects. Firms were asked to submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) showing the necessary qualifications, experience, and workforce to perform the services. The listed firms are recommended to be pre-qualified as labor compliance service providers for a period of three years, September 2017 to September 2020. The Multi-Year Labor Compliance Agreements will permit City staff to issue Task Orders for individual projects. This process will expedite the completion of Council approved projects.

PH 1. Appeal of Planning Commission's Approval of Construction and Operation of a 583,000 Square-Foot Medical Cannabis Cultivation and Manufacturing Facility on 32 Acres at the Southeast Corner of William J. Barnes Avenue and 47th Street West within Specific Plan No. 95-02 (Fox Field Industrial Corridor Specific Plan)
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. 17-42, denying the appeal of the Planning Commission action, and approving Conditional Use Permit No. 17-16.
Conditional Use Permit No. 17-16 is one of four medical cannabis cultivation and manufacturing facilities that have been submitted, reviewed, and acted on by the City since the adoption of Chapters 5.56 and 17.43 of the Lancaster Municipal Code (LMC). All submitted applications undergo a screening and evaluation process to ensure that the required information and materials have been provided prior to the conditional use permit application being reviewed and processed by the Development Services Department and considered by the Planning Commission. Conditional Use Permit No. 17-16 went through this screening and evaluation procedure. The Planning Commission considered Conditional Use Permit No. 17-16 at the meeting of August 14, 2017, and adopted a resolution (by a 5-0-0-1-0 vote) approving the application.

NB 1. Ordinance related to Senate Bill 415 (SB 415) requiring change in Election date
Recommendation:
Introduce Ordinance No. 1033, moving the date of the City's General Municipal Election from the second Tuesday in April of even-numbered years to the first Tuesday after the first Monday in _______________ of even-numbered years beginning _______________, 20____ and amending section 2.040.020 of the Lancaster Municipal Code pertaining to the selection of the Vice Mayor.
SB 415 allows the City to continue to hold its elections in April of even-numbered years as long as by January 1, 2018 the City has "adopted a plan to consolidate a future election with a statewide election not later than the November 8, 2022, Statewide General Election." Once adopted, the City Clerk will forward the Ordinance to the Los Angeles Board of Supervisors for its approval.
